note: Adapted from Snyder 1926; the original is in English. The original treated the species as Armitermes (Armitermes) chagresi Snyder and states that the species was described from the soldier in 1924; the present account covers the first alate collected (in the same nest as soldiers and nymphs, Estrella, Costa Rica, 26 August 1925 (month 8), collected by H. Kirby, Jr.); this part of the original describes the alate only.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The head is pale greyish brown, punctate in appearance because each hair base has a pale spot, and the base of the antennae is paler; the head is broadly oval and densely covered with long hairs. The frontal gland opening is transparent and large but smaller than an ocellus, nearly oval and sunken; the area around the frontal gland opening is paler. The compound eyes are black, large and projecting, close to the lateral margin of the head; the ocelli are transparent, large, nearly oval and projecting, close to the compound eyes. The postclypeus is yellow, arched and bilobed; the labrum is yellow. The antennae are pale yellowish brown, 15-segmented, gradually longer towards the apex, segment 3 only slightly longer than segment 2 or segment 4, and the apical segment slender and nearly elliptical. The pronotum is paler than the head, its posterior margin concave and its sides rounded posteriorly, densely covered with long hairs. The wings are transparent, the costal area and the basal veins darker (yellow to pale yellowish brown), the membranous part densely covered with short hairs; the media of the forewing lies closer to the cubitus and far from the subcosta, with branches running towards the wing apex; the cubitus lies slightly below the Malpighian tube and does not reach the wing apex. Measurements: body length with wings 11.5—11.75 mm; body length after dealation 6.15 mm; head length including the labrum 1.35 mm; pronotum length 0.6 mm; forewing length 9.5 mm; length of the hind tibia 1.7 mm; long diameter of the compound eye 0.45 mm; head width including the compound eyes 1.2 mm; forewing width 3.3 mm; pronotum width 1.05 mm.
